original_question: Determine whether a mechanism analogous to the proposed chamber-and-damper apparatus can explain cascades in real hydrodynamics, and whether one can choose the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i so that the model functions as intended, ideally with an analogue in two-dimensional ideal fluid flow.
target_in_paper: Problem 40 in Section 15.3, "A Model of the Inverse Cascade." ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the chamber-and-damper device, the parameter triple (n_i, m_i, r_i), the question about whether an analogous mechanism exists in real hydrodynamics, and the paper's further interest in a 2D ideal-fluid analogue. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
missing_details: The target is specifically the inverse-cascade problem of Section 15.3, not hydrodynamic cascades in general and not the neighboring dissipation question of Problem 39. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

To make the question stand alone, you need the apparatus itself: a countable family of chambers C_1, C_2, ..., each chamber C_i containing n_i equal elastic balls B_j^i of radius r_i and mass m_i; a vertical wall splitting each chamber into left and right rooms; an upper and a lower door; a spring-loaded shutter at the lower door; and a damper coupled to balls in the next chamber C_{i+1}. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The paper builds in the intended parameter regime: the balls in C_{i+1} should be much smaller and much more numerous than those in C_i, namely m_{i+1} << m_i, r_{i+1} << r_i, and n_{i+1} >> n_i, so that C_{i+1} acts as an effective cooler/viscous gas for the shutter. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The reverse-side transfer mechanism also matters: a turbine driven by the ball stream in C_i, with a ratchet-and-pawl and a stirrer, is supposed to transfer energy to much larger and fewer balls in C_{i-1}, with m_{i-1} >> m_i, r_{i-1} >> r_i, and n_{i-1} << n_i. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

"Works as intended" should be stated explicitly: on average, energy is transferred from chamber C_i toward lower-index chambers and ends up concentrated in the first few chambers, which is the mechanical analogue of the inverse cascade (earlier framed as concentration in lower modes / first few wheels). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

If you keep the 2D clause, it should match the paper's scope: the authors ask, more specifically, whether a similar mechanism works in a 2D ideal fluid, thus ensuring inverse energy cascade there. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

There are no paper-relevant algebraic data here such as ambient ring/field, operator definitions, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, or a phrase like "for all sufficiently large m"; the omitted details are mechanical and dynamical rather than algebraic. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
refined_question: For the countable-chamber apparatus of Section 15.3—where each chamber C_i contains n_i identical elastic balls of mass m_i and radius r_i, the lower door has a spring-loaded one-way shutter damped by interactions with the much smaller and more numerous balls in C_{i+1}, and a turbine/ratchet/stirrer mechanism is intended to transfer energy from the ball stream in C_i to the much larger and fewer balls in C_{i-1}—can one choose the sequences (n_i, m_i, r_i) so that the apparatus indeed produces, on average, transfer of energy toward lower-index chambers and concentration of energy in the first few chambers, thereby realizing the intended inverse-cascade mechanism; and does a similar mechanism exist in real hydrodynamics, preferably already for a 2D ideal fluid?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation, and the phrases "chamber-and-damper apparatus," "n_i, m_i, r_i," and "two-dimensional ideal fluid" make Problem 40 the unmistakable target. The only substantial sharpening needed is to state that the paper is asking about an inverse-cascade mechanism in the exact countable-chamber model defined just before Problem 40, and to unpack what "works as intended" means in that model. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
